idiom_name: duck-typed node objects with a children array (DOM Node as the platform instance)
implementation_notes: JavaScript needs no common base type: any object that answers the operation is a component, so a container is an object (or class instance) holding a children array that delegates recursively, and a leaf is simply the object with no children. The platform already ships the canonical instance - every DOM object implements the Node interface, Element nodes contain other Nodes while Text nodes are leaves, and appendChild/childNodes are the uniform interface - which is why composing DOM subtrees is the everyday form of this pattern. Keep a shared base class or an explicit isContainer() flag when you must reliably distinguish structure-editing operations; duck typing alone cannot tell a leaf from a container.
pitfalls: A leaf missing the expected method fails only when the operation runs, deep inside the recursion - duck typing converts a design error into a runtime TypeError.
DOM childNodes (and children) are live collections: mutating the tree while iterating them skips or repeats nodes, so snapshot them first.
Sharing one array between several containers aliases the subtrees; building nodes with factory functions that copy their input avoids the surprise.
